articles.title: Brewers parade to celebrate 2026 World Series title set for Friday
articles.summary: The Brewers clinched the first World Series in franchise history on Wednesday night against the Rays.
articles.body:
Milwaukee will get its first sports championship-related parade since 2021 on Friday when the Brewers celebrate their 2026 World Series title.

Five years after the Bucks delivered an NBA championship, the Brewers and their fans will have their opportunity to continue to revel in the team's first World Series title (and the city's second after the 1957 Braves) with a Parade of Champions beginning at 11 a.m. ET.

Two days after the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to clinch the series in Game 5, the Commissioner's Trophy will be in attendance as the festivities are set to run through downtown Milwaukee and conclude at Henry Maier Festival Park.

During his postgame press conference, Brewers manager Pat Murphy jokingly asked two of his sons, Austin and Jaxon, whether their little league baseball duties might interfere with attending the parade.

Pat, Austin and Jaxon will be joined by team alumni during the festivities. There will also be a special showing of "Ueck," the documentary about legendary Brewers broadcaster Bob Uecker.

There will also be a Championship Rally at American Family Insurance Amphitheater inside the park.

Should some fans be unable to attend, the parade will be streamed on MLB Network, MLB and Brewers.com.

articles.title: 2026 MLB Free Agents Rumors, Predictions for Tarik Skubal, Brandon Lowe, More
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are your 2026 World Series champions, which can only mean one thing.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are your 2026 World Series champions, which can only mean one thing.

The MLB offseason has officially arrived.

The Brewers might be celebrating still, and the Tampa Bay Rays have joined a few different teams at various stages of the grief process, but all 30 front offices have reached roster-building time.

So, let's put a spotlight on some possible roster-building manuevers and dig into the latest buzz around baseball's free agents.

The Pittsburgh Pirates' trade for Brandon Lowe last offseason could not have gone any better. In fact, you could argue it went a little too well, since his offensive production (35 homers, 96 RBI) and defensive improvement seemingly positioned him for the kind of pay raise that could price out Pittsburgh.

If that was the fear for Pirates fans, a recent contract projection from The Athletic's Jim Bowden (a former MLB executive) landed lower than expected: three years, $45 million. Bowden also listed the Pirates as one of Lowe's three best team fits, along with the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres.

If that's all it takes to get Lowe's signature on the dotted line, the Pirates should be ready to pounce. He's had some availability issues in his past, but if those are behind him (284 games played the past two seasons), a new contract could be heavy on rewards and light on risks.

That just doesn't seem like it will be enough—in annual salary, or in years. And if his actual contract value climbs higher, it probably will force a departure from Pittsburgh and steer him toward a deeper-pocketed club with an opening on the infield.

Prediction: Lowe signs with the New York Yankees.

For all of the unknowns in this MLB offseason, the clearest certainty is that a colossal contract (very possibly a record-setting one) is coming Tarik Skubal's way.

He isn't necessarily a perfect free agent, what with his 30th birthday fast approaching and the fact he had to navigate around elbow surgery this season. That said, his previous two campaigns featured Cy Young awards, and this one showed similar dominance ( 2.51 FIP this year; 2.45 and 2.49 in 2025 and 2024, respectively).

He'll send this market in a frenzy. Every big-spender—starting with the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets—will at least weigh making a bid, and surprise suitors could surface, too. That said, cold water is already getting dumped on the idea of Skubal heading back to the Detroit Tigers.

"It's probably too early to handicap this as Mets versus Dodgers," ESPN's Alden Gonzalez wrote. "... Others will surely step up—though it seems highly unlikely that the Tigers, who never made an extension offer Skubal's side deemed competitive, will be among them."

While that would have been a fun way for this story to end, it never felt too feasible. Because, in all likelihood, it probably isn't too early to consider this a two-team race between New York and L.A.

Prediction: Skubal re-signs with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The Chicago Cubs knew they were headed for a busy offseason given the number of free agents on their roster, but they just had even more business added to their to-do list.

Per ESPN's Jesse Rogers , Clay Holmes and Matthew Boyd will both decline options to enter free agency. They'll also see a lot of familiar faces from this rotation when they get there, since Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman and David Peterson are on the open market as well.

Holmes, acquired in a trade deadline deal with the New York Mets, pitched to a 3.29 ERA over 101.1 innings split between the teams. Boyd, meanwhile, had a 3.91 ERA and 1.21 WHIP in his 126.2 innings.

Of the five pitchers listed above, Rogers opined that one or two "could return." That feels about right, since the Cubs need to upgrade their rotation while also addressing other holes on the roster.

Prediction: Holmes and Peterson re-sign with the Cubs.

articles.title: Important 2026-2027 offseason dates
articles.summary: Look for a lot of activity in November.
articles.body:
With 2026 baseball officially behind us, and so much speculation and insecurity around 2027 baseball, we are now entering that liminal space between seasons that may wind up lasting far longer than any of us would like. We will be with you throughout all of it, however long it lasts, and to begin the official offseason coverage, we're going to take a look at some important dates for the Mets and Major League Baseball as a whole.

At the end of the season, the Mets had zero (0) free agents. Every single player that was due to hit free agency today was traded (or claimed off waivers) during the season. And so the 9am deadline came and went without any Mets activity at all.

In terms of the internal machinations, the Mets have no Qualifying Offers to issue. The Mets currently have three players on the 60-day Injured List who will need to rejoin the 40-Man roster (Tylor Megill, Reed Garrett, and Jorge Polanco). Bo Bichette is the only Met with a player option, so he will have to make a decision about his future in Queens by Monday evening.

With the lockout expected to begin less than a month from now, look for free agency to happen quite quickly.

These are usually fairly tame, in terms of trades and signings, compared to the Winter Meetings, but with those in question, look for the GM meetings to be a hotbed of activity.

Deadline for players to accept the Qualifying Offer, 4 pm ET

Rule 5 protection deadline (Players need to be added to 40-man roster to protect from the Rule 5 draft)

With the Mets needing to add some minor leaguers to their 40-man roster, expect a flurry of releases and trades to make some room before this deadline. Our Lukas Vlahos did a great job of outlining where the Mets' roster stands at the end of the season.

Expect to see a lot of cigars lit with $100 bills and other signs of excess while crying poverty.

See the note about the Rule 5 deadline above.

CBA Expires 11:59 pm ET – Lockout begins

This is the big one; even if things go better than any of us expect, there will likely still be a lockout starting on December 1st.

December 7-9 : Winter Meetings in San Diego

January 8 : Arbitration Figures Exchanged

The Winter Meetings almost certainly won't happen, and the others in this category will be postponed until the lockout ends.

This will be the only real activity between the lockout's beginning and end.

The Mets have three players – Luis Torrens, Nolan McLean, and Carson Benge – who are Gold Glove finalists. The award announcements will be exclusively revealed via ESPN at 9pm EST.

HOF eight-person Contemporary Baseball Era ballot for managers, executives and umpires Silver Slugger Award finalists announced – 2 pm ET

The Mets look to have at least one Rookie of the Year candidate, but seem unlikely have any finalists in any other categories (Cy Young, MVP, Manager of the Year). These will be announced on an MLB Network broadcast from 6pm-8pm.

Heart & Hustle Awards announced – TBD – MLB Network Gold Glove Awards dinner in NYC – Platinum Glove winners announced

Rookie of the Year – 7-8 pm ET (MLB Network)

It seems likely that Carson Benge and/or Nolan McLean get votes in the Rookie of the Year category, with Benge being the Met frontrunner.

Manager of the Year – 7-8 pm ET (MLB Network)

The Mets had two managers this year and neither seems likely to grab any votes here.

Cy Young Awards and BBWAA relievers of year – 7-8 pm ET (MLB Network)

MLB Awards show – 9-11pm ET (MLB Network)

Mariano Rivera & Trevor Hoffman relievers of year Edgard Martinez DH of year

I suppose there is a chance that a Met picks up an honor on the first or second team, but that seems like the only likely Mets action here.

In what world would a 2026 Mets be an MVP candidate?

Hall of Fame announces its 2027 ballot, 12 pm ET – Writer's ballot

Bobby Abreu, David Wright, and Francisco Rodriguez will all be on this ballot, with potential ex-Mets Asdrubal Cabrera, Todd Frazier, and Jay Bruce potentially looking at debuts on the ballot.

BBWAA announces Contemporary Baseball Era inductees

Hall of Fame announces BBWAA voting results & 2007 inductees, 6 p ET (MLB Network)

articles.title: Dominican Appeals Court Revokes Wander Franco Pardon in Sex Abuse Case
articles.summary: SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic (AP) — An appeals court in the Dominican Republic on Thursday granted a request by prosecutors to revoke a judicial pardon previously awarded to Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Wander Franco after he was convicted for the sexual and psychological abuse of a minor.
articles.body:
SANTO DOMINGO, Dominican Republic (AP) — An appeals court in the Dominican Republic on Thursday granted a request by prosecutors to revoke a judicial pardon previously awarded to Tampa Bay Rays shortstop Wander Franco after he was convicted for the sexual and psychological abuse of a minor.

The Dominican Public Prosecutor's Office argued that the lower court's original pardon rested on an erroneous interpretation of legal provisions intended only for exceptional circumstances — conditions that prosecutors maintained do not apply to Franco's case.

Franco's defense team objected to the motion, but the appellate court ruled in favor of the prosecution, essentially upholding Franco's previous conviction, with a suspended three-year prison sentence. Franco will not be required to serve time in custody provided he maintains a fixed residence and remains under judicial supervision.

Franco was arrested in January 2024 after being accused of having a four-month relationship with a girl who was 14 at the time and transferring thousands of dollars to her mother to consent to the illegal relationship . Franco, now 25, was originally convicted in June of 2025.

Six months after that, Tampa Bay placed him on the restricted list, which cut off the pay he had been receiving while on administrative leave. He hasn't played in the majors since. Tampa Bay was eliminated from the World Series last night by the Milwaukee Brewers.

The court on Thursday imposed the conditional terms considering Franco's age and to support his eventual reintegration into society. If he fails to comply with any of the conditions, he will be required to serve the full three-year prison sentence.

Neither Franco nor his legal counsel offered statements to the press upon leaving the courthouse.

Franco, who was once the Ray's star shortstop, had signed a $182 million, 11-year contract in November 2021 but saw his career abruptly halted in August 2023 after authorities in the Dominican Republic announced they were investigating him for an alleged relationship with a minor. Franco was 22 at the time.

Following Thursday's hearing, prosecutors reiterated that they had substantiated their charges throughout multiple trials, presenting robust evidence that established the criminal conduct of both Franco and the minor's mother.

The court upheld a 10-year prison sentence for the mother, who was found guilty of commercial sexual exploitation and money laundering.

Additionally, the court ordered the forfeiture of approximately $34,000 found in her possession — funds provided by Franco in exchange for her consent to his relationship with her daughter.

Franco retains the right to appeal this decision to the Supreme Court of Justice of the Dominican Republic.

Major League Baseball declined to comment.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers broke baseball on their way to remarkably dominant World Series run
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers went 11-2 in the postseason and never trailed in a series, but their dominant World Series run reveals a truth about baseball.
articles.body: The Milwaukee Brewers are 2026 World Series champions, bringing home the organization's first ever title. For the franchise and their fans, it was the culmination of years of quality scouting, drafting, international signings, player development, and remarkably successful trades. It was also a near-perfect example of what it takes to win a championship in baseball. While William Contreras won World Series MVP, voters had plenty of options to choose from on the Milwaukee roster. Jackson Chourio became the first player since Babe Ruth, yes, literally Babe Ruth, to have 10 hits in the first four games of a World Series. Cooper Pratt, a light-hitting, defense-first shortstop, set a rookie record with hits in six straight at bats from game four to game five. BREWERS RIDE RIDICULOUS, RECORD-SETTING EIGHT-RUN INNING TO DOMINANT 3-0 WORLD SERIES LEAD OVER RAYS Brice Turang hit .316, below average hitter David Hamilton crushed what looked like a huge home run in game four. Aaron Ashby went 5.2 innings with no runs, just one hit allowed and nine strikeouts. Abner Uribe allowed just two hits in 5 innings. Jacob Misiorowski allowed only one run in 10.2 innings, winning game one and the clinching game five. Robert Gasser was equally unhittable, with just one run allowed in his game three start. A start so incredible that it was the first of its type by a left-handed pitcher since legendary Hall of Famer Sandy Koufax. The whole team was World Series MVP. The whole team was NLCS MVP, and NLDS MVP too. Milwaukee went 11-2 in the postseason against the San Diego Padres, the hottest team in baseball in the second half, the star-studded 100-win Los Angeles Dodgers, and the 98-win Tampa Bay Rays, who tore through the American League. They won eight straight games in the playoffs. Their two losses came by a combined two runs, and their one World Series loss was on a walk-off in the 12th inning after they blew a 3-2 lead. It's not a stretch to say it's one of the most dominant stretches of playoff baseball in the history of the sport. And it's why we can make the argument that the Milwaukee Brewers broke Major League Baseball. It's not supposed to be this easy, and it rarely is, even for some of the most expensive, talented rosters we've ever seen. The 2024 Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani coming off the first 50-50 season in history and a long list of other stars, were down 2-1 in the NLDS to the Padres before coming back to win. It took them six games to beat the Mets in the NLCS. They very nearly lost the clinching game five of the World Series, falling behind 5-0 to the Yankees before the New York defense went on a comical run of errors and mental mistakes. In 2025, they were down to their final two outs in game seven of the series against Toronto, until Miguel Rojas hit a miraculous game-tying homer. Milwaukee? They never trailed in a series, or even came close. In fact, it was the exact opposite. They had a 2-0 lead in the NLDS, a 4-0 lead in the NLCS, and a 3-0 lead in the NLCS. It's remarkable. Which raises the question, how did they do it? What was their philosophy and approach in October? The real answer, boring as it might be, they didn't do anything. Baseball happened. That's not to say that the Brewers don't have good players or didn't have good results. Misiorowski is going to win the Cy Young Award at 24-years-old, and looks set to dominate the league for years to come. Christian Yelich is a former MVP, multiple-time Silver Slugger Award winner and borderline candidate for the Hall of Fame. William Contreras has been a top-three catcher in baseball for several years. Garrett Mitchell is a former first round pick and top prospect, as is Brice Turang. Jackson Chourio is already a star at 22. The big secret the Brewers discovered? Have your players get hot at the right time, have a few bounces go your way, rely on some of your less talented players to hit perfectly timed home runs, and sit back and watch as your bullpen goes from very good to almost literally untouchable. Every year, the greater baseball world looks to find some sort of meaning or blueprint from the team that wins the World Series. In 2024 and 2025, the Dodgers "proved" that you can just guarantee a title by spending money, even though the Mets and Yankees haven't won in decades. In 2023, the Rangers showed you need a veteran manager like Bruce Bochy, and that home runs, Texas hit eight in five games, are how you win in October. Very smart analysts have pointed to quality bullpens, big midseason trades, drafting and development, free agency, dominant starting rotations, home runs, or making contact and putting the ball in play. The reality? You need all of those, and you can't predict which ones you'll actually get when it matters. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Not once in these discussions does anyone acknowledge that the different paths taken by different teams demonstrate that there is no one way to win a championship. And that the disparate approaches to roster construction show that what actually matters is a combination of timing, randomness, luck, and talent. Because there has to be meaning and lessons and broad conclusions to draw from every outcome, the baseball world picks a reason and explanation, then quietly discards it when next year's team does the opposite. Here are a few examples of why looking for meaning in playoff baseball is pointless. "Clutch" hitting is frequently praised as meaningful and predictive. Some players just have the "clutch" gene, the received baseball wisdom goes. So let's look at superstar shorstop Corey Seager as an example. Seager had an astonishing run in the 2020 playoffs, hitting. 328 with eight home runs and 20 runs batted in, winning NLCS and World Series MVP. One of the best postseasons ever. Clutch hitter, right? In 2016 and 2017, he went a combined 18 for 82. Then in the 2019 postseason went 3-20 with two singles and no homers. In 2021, Seager was 9-48, a .188 batting average. In 2023, he was once again a force of nature for Texas, hitting .318 with six homers. So is Seager the clutch playoff force from 2020 and 2023, or the hopeless, unclutch, "moment is too big" failure from 2016, 2017, 2019, and 2021? Corey Seager is an elite hitter, but even the best hitters go through hot and cold streaks. Pitchers go through hot and cold streaks. They can't pick and choose when those streaks happen, because if they could, they'd all pick to be hot in October. Derek Jeter hit .235 in the 1998 playoffs, .226 in the 2001 playoffs, .245 in 2004, .176 in 2007, and .250 in 2010 and 2011. He also had plenty of very good results in other years. That's baseball. Aaron Ashby quite literally had the greatest October by a relief pitcher in baseball history. Next year, he could be the worst pitcher on the team in the NLDS. That's baseball. Robert Gasser could be horrible next season after his dominance in this year's playoffs. That's baseball. Look at last year's Toronto Blue Jays. Ernie Clement, literally Ernie Clement, set the record for most hits in a single postseason with an incredible 30 in 73 at bats. In 2026, he was 20% worse than league average offensively, cost his team 14 runs compared to an average hitter, and had a .285 on base percentage. In the 2025 playoffs, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. had a .356 batting average on balls in play. Addison Barger was .422, Ernie Clement was .420, and George Springer .319. Predictably, the Blue Jays scored a lot of runs in October. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER In 2026, Guerrero had a .288 BABIP, Springer was .282, Clement .272, and Barger was .063 in his few games before he got hurt. Toronto finished in last place and missed the playoffs. That is also baseball. There's no predictive value from the tournament, because players do not magically become different in October. There's just a typical distribution of outcomes, particularly among good teams, that sometimes goes your way and sometimes doesn't. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD None of this means the Brewers didn't deserve to win, or weren't a good team. They absolutely did, and they absolutely are. They deserve an immense amount of credit for identifying players in the draft or international markets, as well as in trades and free agency, that they thought they could improve or would fit specific needs. But looking for some sort of explanation or path for your favorite team to follow is insane. Because while you need good players to win, you can't predict how they'll perform over a few weeks of small sample sizes. It's just...baseball. Enjoy it when your team wins, celebrate it, and understand that the inherent variability of it ensures it can't ever be broken.

articles.title: Pitcher Michael King opts out of contract, $61 million with Padres for free agency
articles.summary: King was 10th among National League starting pitchers with a 3.21 ERA and allowed 1 run in 14 innings versus the World Series champion Brewers during the NLD...
articles.body:
Starting pitcher Michael King opted out of his $32 million player option for 2027 with the San Diego Padres and will become a free agent, according to reports.

In their ranking of the top 50 free agents in Major League Baseball this offseason, Yahoo Sports' Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman placed King as the fifth-best player available and third-best starting pitcher behind Tarik Skubal and Freddy Peralta.

King, who will turn 32 on May 25, compiled a 3.21 ERA this past season, ranking 10th among National League starters. He finished with a 12-10 record in 32 starts with 159 strikeouts in 185 innings.

That rate of 7.7 strikeouts per nine innings is King's lowest since becoming a full-time starting pitcher in 2024 after joining the Padres as part of the package the New York Yankees traded for Juan Soto .

King also had a strong postseason, making two starts in which he allowed 1 run with 14 strikeouts in 12 innings versus the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Division Series. The right-hander also made a relief appearance in Game 3, pitching 2 innings to earn the save in San Diego's lone win .

For his career, King has a 3.23 ERA in 143 appearances (96 starts) with a strikeout rate of 9.5 per nine frames. He pitched three seasons with the Padres, preceded by five years with the Yankees.

The eight-year veteran signed a three-year, $75 million contract last December that included opt-outs after the first two seasons. King leaves $66 million behind after choosing free agency, though he receives a $5 million buyout. Obviously, he feels he will make more on the open market amid a mediocre class of starting pitchers.

Unless King re-signs with the Padres, their starting rotation is thin as the offseason begins with Robbie Ray, Casey Mize, Lucas Giolito and Walker Buehler all free agents. Yu Darvish has two years remaining on his contract, but is considering retirement .

articles.title: Jacob Misiorowski's Hat, Ashby's Glasses & All Brewers Artifacts Added to HOF After World Series Run
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday evening.

Items from their Fall Classic run will now be donated to the National Baseball Hall of Fame, including ace pitcher Jacon Misiorowski's Game 5 hat and left-handed reliever Aaron Ashby's iconic glasses.

Top Photos From Brewers' World Series Win

Catcher (and World Series MVP) William Contreras' chest protector and shinguards

Left-handed reliever Aaron Ashby's glasses

Right fielder Sal Frelick's Game 2 batting gloves

Left fielder Christian Yelich's Game 4 jersey

Shortstop Cooper Pratt's Game 4 and 5 bat

Starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski's Game 5 cap

Second baseman Brice Turang's Game 5 cleats

All of the items are significant, of course.

Contreras was a defensive wizard behind the plate, throwing out four runners and guiding a fantastic Brewers staff that allowed just 12 runs over five games. He also fared well in his ABS challenge efforts, with 10 of his 13 calls overturned.

Manager Pat Murphy was promoted from bench coach to manager when Craig Counsell left town for the Chicago Cubs three years ago, and he's since led the Brewers to three NL Central titles and win totals of 93, 97 and 103.

This year's team was the best of all, of course, and is just one of eight teams in the past 40 years to win 100 or more regular season games and the World Series in the same year.

Ashby threw 18 scoreless innings in these playoffs, striking out 20 while allowing just five hits and three walks. Right fielder Sal Frelick hit a game-tying solo home run in Game 2 to help turn a 4-0 first-inning deficit into a 5-4 win.

Left fielder Christian Yelich, the Brewers' captain, has been with the team for nine seasons. He's made three All-Star Games and won the National League MVP in 2018.

Pratt was sensational in Games 4 and 5. He nearly was the hero in Game 4, hitting a solo homer in the top of the 12th to give Milwaukee a 3-2 lead before Tampa Bay came back for a 4-3 win. That gave him four hits. Pratt then added two RBI and a run in Game 5.

Misiorowski, the presumptive National League Cy Young winner, threw 5.2 shutout innings in Game 5, putting the Brewers in an advantageous position for the series clincher.

Second baseman Brice Turang had a pair of hits (including a double) and a run in Game 5. His 100 RBI this season led the team.

articles.title: Bo Bichette Makes Decision on Mets Contract Option in New Rumors with $84M Left on Deal
articles.summary: Coming off a disappointing 2026 season, Bo Bichette is staying with the New York Mets as he looks to rebound next year.
articles.body:
Coming off a disappointing 2026 season, Bo Bichette is staying with the New York Mets as he looks to rebound next year.

Per Will Sammon of The Athletic, Bichette will opt in to his $42 million salary for the 2027 season to remain with the Mets. The infielder is also owed $42 million in 2028, but will have another chance to opt out next winter.

1 Player Every Team Must Re-Sign in Free Agency 💰

Everything to Know on Lockout and Key Upcoming Dates ⚾

One of the top free agents last offseason, Bichette signed a unique three-year, $126 million contract to join the Mets in January 2026. He has opt-outs after each of the first two seasons, potentially giving him the opportunity to secure a longer-term deal.

It seemed apparent very early in the 2026 campaign that Bichette would decide to stay with the Mets given his struggles at the plate. He hit .255/.300/.376 prior to the All-Star break.

Things did improve for Bichette after the break with a .267/.329/.411 slash line, but it was highly unlikely he would be able to get a contract on the open market anywhere close to the money he will get by opting in.

Bichette has been up and down over the past three seasons. His 2024 campaign was limited to just 81 games due to injuries, then he bounced back in 2025 with a .311/.357/.483 slash line in 139 games to help the Toronto Blue Jays win the AL East.

A knee injury kept Bichette out for the first two rounds of the playoffs, but he returned to post a .923 OPS in the World Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Despite a difficult 2026 season, Bichette and the Mets have reasons to be optimistic about a bounce back in 2027. He is only 28 and was also learning to play a new position at third base because Francisco Lindor is entrenched at shortstop in Queens.

If the Mets get the best version of Bichette next season, it will provide a huge boost as they look to get back to being a playoff contender in the NL.

articles.title: 2-time All-Star Bo Bichette reportedly opting in for $42M to return to Mets in 2027
articles.summary: With the threat of a lockout looming while coming off a relatively down season, Bichette reportedly opted for the security of a $42 million deal rather than...
articles.body:
Bo Bichette is ready to run it back with the New York Mets.

The two-time All-Star infielder intends to exercise a $42 million player option to return to the Mets for the 2027 season, The Athletic reports .

Bichette joined the Mets last offseason as one of the prized free agents in his class after seven standout seasons with the Toronto Blue Jays. He signed a three-year $126 million contract with player options for 2027 and 2028.

When he joined the Mets, they were eyeing contention for a World Series title in 2026. The Mets instead were arguably the biggest disappointment in baseball with a 74-88 record and last-place finish in the NL East.

Bichette, 28, got off to a slow start in his first season with New York, but rallied to finish with a .260/.312/.390 slash line with 18 home runs and 78 RBI. The full-season production was below the All-Star standard he set with the Blue Jays, but he flashed his former All-Star form late in the season.

With the threat of a lockout looming while coming off a relatively down season, Bichette opted for the security of a $42 million deal rather than risk going into a work stoppage without a contract. He maintains his player option for 2028 and could command more value on a longer deal next offseason if he returns to his All-Star form.

The Mets, meanwhile, are hoping Bichette can contribute to a turnaround in 2027 when and if baseball is actually played.

articles.title: Dustin May's Decision on Brewers Contract Option Revealed in New Rumors After Winning World Series
articles.summary: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May will become a free agent after declining his mutual option for the 2027 MLB season on Thursday, according to Jon Heyman of the New York Post.
articles.body:
Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May will become a free agent after declining his mutual option for the 2027 MLB season on Thursday, according to Jon Heyman of the New York Post .

The mutual option was worth $20 million (via Spotrac ).

May's decision comes one day after the Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays in five games to win the 2026 World Series, capturing their first championship in franchise history.

He opened the 2026 season with the St. Louis Cardinals before he was sent to Milwaukee in an Aug. 3 trade .

The Brewers received May and left-handed reliever JoJo Romero from St. Louis in exchange for minor league outfielders Alexander Frías and Josiah Ragsdale.

May started 21 games for the Cardinals prior to the trade, posting a 7-9 record to go along with a 4.38 ERA and 1.284 WHIP. He also recorded 106 strikeouts compared to 35 walks in 109 innings of work.

The 29-year-old's production dipped following the change of scenery, as he compiled a 5.65 ERA across 10 starts with the Brewers. Opposing batters also posted a .796 OPS against May during his time in Milwaukee.

He was primarily utilized as a bullpen piece during the Brewers' ensuing playoff run, allowing 11 hits and seven earned runs in 11 innings pitched.

Teams looking to sign May in free agency will hope that he can put his struggles in 2026 behind him, as he owned a 3.86 career ERA prior to this season.

articles.title: Baseball May NEVER See Anything Like This Again! Jackson Chourio and William Contreras Just Conquered the Entire Sport in One INSANE Season!

articles.body:
What Jackson Chourio and William Contreras have accomplished in 2026 is almost impossible to put into words. These two Milwaukee Brewers stars have experienced a season that most professional baseball players can only dream about, collecting championships, breaking records and dominating on the biggest stages in the sport.

And somehow, they saved their best moments for October.

It all started with the World Baseball Classic. Chourio and Contreras helped Venezuela capture its first WBC championship, giving them an international title before the MLB regular season had even begun. They would eventually add another championship to their resumes just seven months later.

The Brewers followed up their international success with an incredible regular season, finishing with 103 wins — the best record in all of baseball and a franchise record.

Chourio, at just 22 years old, put together another outstanding campaign, hitting .291 with 25 home runs, 75 RBIs, 96 runs scored and 23 stolen bases. Contreras was equally important, batting .270 with 18 home runs, 94 RBIs and 153 hits while serving as the leader behind the plate.

Milwaukee wasn't just winning games. It was building one of the most dominant teams in baseball.

The postseason started with a four-game battle against the Padres, and both players delivered.

Contreras hit .375 with two home runs, two RBIs and a 1.194 OPS across the series. His power was on full display, including a go-ahead home run in Game 1.

Chourio had a quieter series at the plate overall, hitting .188, but he came through in the biggest moment of Game 2. With Milwaukee down to its final opportunity, he delivered a walk-off two-run single to give the Brewers a 2-0 series lead.

Milwaukee eventually finished the job in Game 4, advancing with a 3-1 series victory.

Next came the defending champions, and Milwaukee made them look completely helpless.

The Brewers swept Los Angeles in four games, getting revenge for their previous postseason disappointment against the Dodgers.

Contreras continued his incredible postseason, batting .357 with five hits, a home run, three RBIs and a 1.113 OPS. His Game 2 performance was especially impressive, delivering a game-tying home run before adding another go-ahead hit as Milwaukee took control.

Chourio struggled more in this series, hitting .158 with one home run and one RBI, but his overall postseason contributions were still important to Milwaukee's championship run.

The Brewers completed the sweep with a 6-4 victory in Game 4, punching their ticket to the World Series.

This is where Chourio and Contreras put the finishing touches on an unforgettable season.

At just 22 years old, Chourio absolutely exploded against Tampa Bay. He hit .458 in the World Series, collecting 11 hits through the first four games. That tied Babe Ruth for the most hits through the first four games of a World Series.

He also became the youngest player to record a four-hit World Series game since 1946, doing it at 22 years and 229 days old. He finished the series with 11 hits, four runs scored and two RBIs.

Contreras was just as important, and his impact went far beyond the batter's box.

He hit .381 with four RBIs across the five games, including a run-scoring single in Game 1 and a crucial RBI double in the deciding Game 5. Behind the plate, he threw out four attempted base stealers and consistently controlled Tampa Bay's running game. He also won 10 of his 13 challenges using MLB's Automated Ball-Strike system.

When the final out was recorded in Milwaukee's 4-1 series victory, Contreras was named World Series MVP — becoming the first player in Brewers history to win the award.

A season that belongs in baseball history

Think about everything these two have accomplished in a single calendar year.

World Baseball Classic champions with Venezuela.

MLB's best regular-season record at 103 wins.

A National League Division Series victory over San Diego.

A four-game sweep of the defending champion Dodgers.

World Series champions after defeating Tampa Bay in five games.

William Contreras taking home World Series MVP.

Jackson Chourio making history at just 22 years old.

The Brewers finished the postseason 11-2, losing just two games on their way to the franchise's first World Series championship.

There are great seasons, there are championship seasons, and then there is what Chourio and Contreras just accomplished.

Two championships in one year, a historic regular season, record-breaking postseason moments and a World Series MVP.

articles.title: Watch Brewers Players Celebrate World Series with Lambeau Leaps in Video at Packers vs. Panthers
articles.summary: A day after winning their first World Series in franchise history, the Milwaukee Brewers celebrated at Lambeau Field.
articles.body:
A day after winning their first World Series in franchise history, the Milwaukee Brewers celebrated at Lambeau Field.

Several members of the Brewers made an appearance at Lambeau for the Green Bay Packers matchup against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday. Their celebrations included some Lambeau Leaps.

Top Photos From Brewers' World Series Win

The Brewers had a magical season, finishing with a franchise-record 103 wins before coasting through the postseason. They downed the San Diego Padres in five games, swept the Los Angeles Dodgers and beat the Tampa Bay Rays in five games in the World Series.

William Contreras took home the World Series MVP after hitting .381 with an .864 OPS and four RBI.

The Brewers, founded in 1969, reached the World Series in 1982, where they lost to the St. Louis Cardinals, and hadn't been back to the Fall Classic until this year. With one title under its belt, Milwaukee is set up for success for years to come and will look to add a few more in the coming years.

The question is whether the Packers can bring Milwaukee sports fans as much joy as the Brewers did this year. Green Bay has had a shaky 4-3 start to the season, losing manageable games against the Minnesota Vikings, Atlanta Falcons and Detroit Lions.

Despite a rough start, the Packers have the talent to make a deep postseason run and perhaps join the Brewers as champions.

articles.title: Brewers present World Series trophy at Packers-Panthers, celebrate with Lambeau Leap
articles.summary: The Brewers have made a triumphant return to Wisconsin after winning their first World Series on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Fresh off the franchise's first World Series victory , the Milwaukee Brewers are ready to celebrate with all of Wisconsin. After beating the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5 on Wednesday, Brewers returned to Milwaukee on Thursday, and made their first major stop at the Green Bay Packers' prime-time matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

During a break after the first quarter of Thursday's game, several players emerged from the tunnel at Lambeau Field with the World Series trophy held high, earning a roar from the Packers crowd.

The Brewers' appearance at Lambeau was slightly spoiled by right fielder Sal Frelick, who joined ESPN's "SportsCenter" for an interview while on the bus to Green Bay. Frelick was candid about how the celebrations had been going since beating the Rays on Wednesday.

"It's been crazy. Not a lot of sleep, late night last night, early bus to the airport this morning. Just got back here to Milwaukee and now we're headed up north," Frelick said, panning to show his teammates, including the trophy-carting ace Jacob Misiorowski.

Once in Lambeau, some Brewers players, including Frelick, then opted to do a Lambeau Leap into the crowd as part of the first-quarter break.

Unfortunately, the Brewers weren't the only players who got a chance to try the Lambeau Leap: On the first play of the second quarter, Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard ran in for a 1-yard touchdown to re-take the lead, and made the Leap in celebration afterward.

In the end the Packers did more celebrating, winning the game 27-19 .

The Brewers will be celebrating with more fans Friday, with a parade planned through downtown Milwaukee .

articles.title: Where to watch the Brewers parade: Start time, TV channels, live streams for Milwaukee World Series celebration
articles.summary: Milwaukee will shut down Friday for a wide-ranging celebration of its long-awaited champions. Here's all you need to know to tune in.
articles.body:
A party decades in the making is set to take over Milwaukee on Friday.

After dominating all comers throughout the regular season and playoffs, the Brewers are World Series champions for the first time. Considering that franchise moved to Milwaukee in 1970 and the city's only previous triumph was the Braves' Fall Classic win over the Yankees in 1957, Friday is shaping up to be an all-time party.

An Associated Press story detailing the welcome the champion Braves got upon returning home from New York 69 years ago describes about 250,000 people crowding into an area two blocks wide and two miles long down Wisconsin Avenue. That's in addition to some 20,000 who reportedly greeted the team at the airport at 7:30 p.m. before they set out on a somewhat impromptu parade of 30 convertibles in 47-degree temperatures with a strong wind off the lake. Photos from that evening show an endless sea of people that forced police to clear a path so the team's vehicles could get through.

Friday's event will be much more organized, with a parade followed by a rally, but the crowd numbers figure to dwarf that long-ago celebration. It will be a day to remember for Milwaukee and Brewers fans everywhere. Here's when and where to watch, no matter where you are.

The Brewers' World Series championship parade is set to begin Friday at 10 a.m. local time, or 11 a.m. ET. The procession will travel through downtown Milwaukee on the way to Henry Maier Festival Park, where a celebration rally will follow. See the full parade route below.

articles.title: Predicting MLB Teams' Qualifying Offers and If Players Accept or Reject
articles.summary: As you've undoubtedly heard a few hundred times over the past couple of months, it is eventually going to be a very atypical offseason for Major League Baseball.
articles.body:
As you've undoubtedly heard a few hundred times over the past couple of months, it is eventually going to be a very atypical offseason for Major League Baseball.

For another month until the inevitable lockout, though, it's still offseason business as usual. And one of the first mile markers in every offseason is the window in which teams extend qualifying offers to free agents-to-be.

We'll discuss shortly what a qualifying offer is, how much it is and who is eligible to receive one, but teams have until Monday afternoon to extend said offers.

We see 10 players as relatively obvious candidates for a QO.

How likely is it that they'll get one, though?

And will they accept or reject the offer?

What Is a Qualifying Offer and Who Is (and Isn't) Eligible to Receive One?

Major League Baseball's qualifying offer is a one-year proposal that a team can make to a player from its roster who is about to become a free agent. The value is determined as the average salary of the league's 125 highest-paid players from the just-completed season. This year, that figure is $23.15M.

Teams have until 5 p.m. ET on Nov. 2 to make qualifying offers. Players who receive one will have until 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 17 to make their decision.

If the player accepts the offer, huzzah, one more year with the same team.

If the player declines the qualifying offer and ultimately signs with a new team, his previous team receives a compensatory draft pick. Where that draft pick lands depends on whether the team contributes to or benefits from revenue sharing and whether they paid a competitive balance tax. How much the player signs for in free agency can also affect the draft pick.

If the player has previously received a qualifying offer—regardless of which team extended that previous offer—he is ineligible to receive another one. Per Spotrac , there are 27 such players this year, including Michael King, Bo Bichette and Nick Martinez, who otherwise would have been top candidates for one.

Also, a qualifying offer can only be extended to a player if he spent the entire season with his current team. In other words, no one who was traded mid-season—i.e. Tarik Skubal, Freddy Peralta, Clay Holmes or Luis Arraez—can receive a qualifying offer.

Because of those restrictions, we might only see a few offers extended this year.

For what it's worth, there were 13 qualifying offers last offseason, four of which—Brandon Woodruff, Trent Grisham, Gleyber Torres and Shota Imanaga—were accepted. (Five, actually, if you want to count Zac Gallen, who initially declined the qualifying offer, but ended up later agreeing to a one-year deal at last year's qualifying offer price of $22.025M.) Prior to that, though, only 14 out of 144 qualifying offers were accepted.

Now, let's talk candidates, in alphabetical order by last name.

Why He's a Candidate for Qualifying Offer

Even before this season, Randy Arozarena was already one of the more valuable position players in baseball. The 2021 AL Rookie of the Year (and viral star of the 2020 postseason) was a .249 hitter from 2021-25, racking up at least 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases in each of those five seasons.

This year, though, he kicked it up a notch. Arozarena set career-best marks (in seasons of at least 25 games) in each of batting average (.281), on-base percentage (.381) and slugging percentage (.484). He also led the American League in runs scored (113) while hitting 26 dingers and swiping 26 bags.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: 100 percent

Simply put, if only one player receives a qualifying offer this week, it's going to be Arozarena. After filtering out the players who are ineligible to receive one, he is hands down the most coveted free agent in this cycle.

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: 0 percent

Whether he ultimately clears $23.15M with his AAV in free agency remains to be seen, but Arozarena (who turns 32 in February) is almost certainly headed for a four-year or five-year deal in free agency, very likely north of $100M in total. There's no chance he's leaving that on the table to stick with Seattle for one more year.

Jake Bauers just had an "out of nowhere" campaign for the ages.

In his first two seasons with the Brewers (2024 and 2025), he was the left-handed half of a platoon situation with Rhys Hoskins at first base, as well as a frequent pinch hitter with an unremarkable .696 OPS. He entered 2026 with a career bWAR of minus-1.2 .

But he became one of the most important pieces of the world champs, both because of his team-leading 26 home runs and .874 OPS and because of his excellent defense at first base.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: 60 percent

Bauers is absolutely headed for a pay raise after making just $2.7M in 2026. An 850 percent increase, though? That might be tough for Milwaukee to justify, regardless of how crucial he was to their cause this season. However, if they're reasonably confident he will turn down the QO and they can get a draft pick out of losing him, why not?

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: 30 percent

On the open market, Bauers should fetch close to a $15M salary on a three- or four-year deal. If Milwaukee is willing and able to offer him something in that ballpark, you have to love the chances of him staying put. It wouldn't be surprising, though, to see him turn down $23M in pursuit of closer to $60M, even at a lower annual salary.

1 Player Every Team Must Re-Sign in Free Agency 💰

MLB Power Rankings Entering 2026-27 Free Agency

In five of the past six seasons, David Bednar has been one of the best relievers in baseball. We're talking a sub-2.70 ERA and sub-2.70 FIP in each of those seasons, as well as a cumulative K/9 north of 11. And in eight career appearances in the postseason, he has a 1.00 ERA.

Even with a very disappointing 2024 campaign factored into the data, he has been a clear-cut top 10 reliever since the beginning of 2021 and figures to be the most coveted bullpen arm in free agency this winter.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: At least 95 percent

New York's bullpen situation is looking rough heading into the offseason, slated to lose just about every high-leverage reliever they had in 2026. They're going to at least try to keep their closer for $23.15M, as it will likely cost more than that to replace him, either in dollars on a different free agent or in prospects in a trade.

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: Less than 10 percent

Josh Hader got a five-year, $95M deal three winters ago. Tanner Scott got a four-year, $72M deal during the 2024-25 offseason. Edwin Díaz has twice signed multi-year contracts with an AAV in excess of $20M. And with 143 saves over the past half-decade, Bednar should be able to command something in the 3-4 years, $18M-$20M AAV ballpark. Hard to imagine he won't decline this QO to pursue that bigger payday.

Even in what was a disappointing walk year by his standards, Jazz Chisholm Jr.'s value added is undeniable. He had 19 home runs and 41 stolen bases and easily could have been named a finalist for the AL 2B Gold Glove award.

Since the beginning of 2024, that brings his totals to 74 home runs and 112 stolen bases—totals almost identical to Bobby Witt Jr.'s marks of 73 and 114, respectively, even though Chisholm has 344 fewer plate appearances during that time.

Granted, that is otherwise an apples and oranges comparison, with Witt the vastly superior defender while also boasting an .880 OPS to Chisholm's .761. But second basemen with 30/30 potential don't exactly grow on trees.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: Less than 10 percent

There's no rule prohibiting a team from extending multiple qualifying offers in the same year. In fact, the Cubs, Padres and Phillies each had two last offseason. But most in the know seem to believe the Yankees will give David Bednar a qualifying offer while declining to extend one to Chisholm. Simply put, they don't need him with middle infielders George Lombard Jr., Anthony Volpe and José Caballero all returning.

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: Almost zero percent

Back in February , Chisholm was talking about seeking a $35M salary on an 8-10 year deal, putting his self-valuation at $280M-$350M in free agency. While there's no chance he'll sniff those numbers after the year he just had, there's also no chance he'd settle for $23.15M without at least finding out what his market looks like.

After nine consecutive seasons with an OPS of at least .757, Ian Happ had a bit of a disappointing year at the dish, striking out more than ever before (189 K) and batting just .218.

He did still hit 24 home runs, though, going for at least 21 HR and 66 RBI for the fifth time in six years. He's also a finalist for what would be his fifth consecutive Gold Glove in left field.

All told, he has been worth 16.1 fWAR since the beginning of 2022, good for top 20 among outfielders .

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: 49 percent

This might be the toughest call of them all. Not only do the Cubs also have Seiya Suzuki as an outfielder who is indisputably even more deserving of a QO, but they need to put in quite a bit of work on their pitching staff this winter. That makes it feel slightly more likely than not that they just let Happ explore free agency without attaching any draft pick compensation to him.

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: 20 percent

Even if he doesn't expect to fetch a $23M salary in free agency, at 32 years old already, this might be Happ's last chance to cash in on a multi-year deal. Given his great defense and his proven consistency as a 20+ homer type of guy, it's plausible he could get a second helping of the three-year, $61M contract he just finished up.

Since the beginning of 2023, there have been four players who primarily play catcher, who have tallied at least 1,600 plate appearances and who have an OPS of at least .780. They are Cal Raleigh, William Contreras, Will Smith and Ryan Jeffers.

Jeffers' consistent production at the plate has flown a bit below the radar because he doesn't hit that many home runs. But he is the creme de la creme of backstops in this winter's class of free agents, if the Twins let him get there.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: 80 percent

This would be closer to 100 percent if the Twins weren't allergic to spending money. But this is somewhat of a do-or-die year for them in terms of the sheer volume of key players who will hit free agency next offseason. If they don't even extend Jeffers a QO, they might as well also put Joe Ryan, Pablo López and others on the trade block while they're at it.

If Jeffers gets a QO and declines it, history says to expect a five-year deal in free agency. Only five catchers have received and declined a qualifying offer, and four of them—Willson Contreras, J.T. Realmuto, Russell Martin and Brian McCann—subsequently inked five-year contracts. And if the Yankees are unable to trade for either Shea Langeliers or Hunter Goodman, they might get desperate enough to make Jeffers a substantial offer.

Brandon Lowe had 35 home runs, 96 RBI and an .824 OPS at second base for the Pirates in 2026, and it wasn't even his most impressive season as a big leaguer.

Heck, for his career, Lowe has an .810 OPS and has averaged 35 home runs and 98 RBI on a 162-games basis. Staying healthy was his struggle for a while in the 2022-24 timeframe, but with 284 games played (and 282 hits to show for it) over the past two seasons, that's much less of a concern than it used to be.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: At least 90 percent

As is, the largest AAV in Pirates history is the $15.55M mark on their nine-year, $140M extension with Konnor Griffin. Even on a one-year deal, going to $23.15M for one player would represent a brave new world in Pittsburgh. But how could they justify not at least trying to bring back Lowe after a season in which he was their most valuable player by a pretty wide margin?

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: 35 percent

Lowe is already 32 years old and has the misfortune of hitting free agency in a year when the market is oversaturated with quality, younger second basemen. Jazz Chisholm Jr., Luis Arraez and Gleyber Torres are all expected to be available, none of whom has yet celebrated turning 30—and there simply aren't that many teams likely to invest a ton of money at second base. I do think he declines the QO and can reasonably expect around $60M on a three-year deal, but it wouldn't exactly be a stunner if he takes this offer.

In qualifying offer history, 10 relief pitchers have received one. All 10—Edwin Díaz, Josh Hader, Raisel Iglesias, Will Smith, Craig Kimbrel, Wade Davis, Greg Holland, Kenley Jansen, David Robertson and Rafael Soriano—were already well-established closers.

So, if Adrián Morejón does receive one with just eight career saves, it'd be a bit of a historic moment.

Over the past three years, however, he has been the most dominant reliever in all of baseball, save for Mason Miller, Cade Smith and maybe Jhoan Duran.

He isn't a closer yet, but it's very likely he is going to be treated as a closer in contract negotiations.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: 40 percent

In a different roster situation, this could be as high as 100 percent. That's how valuable Morejón has been. However, what the Padres desperately need is not more bullpen arms, but starting pitching. And if they get stuck holding a $23.15M bag for a set-up guy for Miller, it'll make it that much harder for them to secure another quality arm for the rotation. They may well extend Morejón a QO, but mostly hoping for the draft pick.

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: 55 percent

For a reliever who made $3.9M this past season and who isn't already a closer, turning down a guaranteed $23.15M could be tough. Established forces like Hader and Díaz had no problem doing so, knowing they'd get close to that on an annual basis on a new contract. But how confident is Morejón that an offer of 4-plus years at a salary of $15M-plus is waiting for him? Especially with all of the uncertainty for Dec. 2 and beyond? He just might take the one-year offer before trying to work on an extension. (And if that happens, get ready for all of the Mason Miller trade speculation.)

There was a seven-start stretch this spring in which Trevor Rogers couldn't string together outs, amassing an ERA slightly north of 10.00 during a run of seven consecutive team losses.

Even with that rough patch included—and even after missing most of the first two months of 2025—Rogers has a 3.16 ERA and a 7.3 fWAR since the beginning of 2025, ranking 17th among all pitchers in the latter department, just barely behind both Cam Schlittler and Drew Rasmussen.

When this southpaw is on, not many are better.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: Close to 100 percent

Getting Rogers to stick around for one more season sure would save the Orioles a lot of trouble this offseason, as they otherwise arguably need to trade for a different short-term, ace-caliber pitcher while they wait for their trio of top pitching prospects to hopefully become fixtures in the starting rotation within the next two years. $23.15M would be the second-highest AAV they've ever given a player, behind only the $31M AAV they signed Pete Alonso to last winter. But they have to at least try.

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: Less than 5 percent

Given his injury history and inconsistent performance, a nine-figure contract offer is hardly guaranteed to come Rogers' way. But it might. At any rate, he hasn't even turned 29 yet, which is relevant in a "best available starting pitchers" pecking order that also includes Michael King and Clay Holmes in advance of their age-32 and age-34 seasons, respectively. Rogers should be able to get at least a three-year deal, and possibly even five years at around $20M apiece.

Seiya Suzuki picked one heck of a time to put together the best season of his career, finishing out a five-year, $85M contract with a bang.

On offense, it was pretty much business as usual. His .841 OPS was almost identical to what he did in both 2023 (.842) and 2024 (.848). With 26 home runs and 86 RBI, it was also his fourth consecutive year with at least 20 and 73, respectively.

But after spending four years as a bit of a liability in right field, there's a chance he'll win the Gold Glove for his work in 2026.

He got overshadowed a bit (OK, a lot) as we all fawned over Pete Crow-Armstrong's NL MVP campaign, but Suzuki was a borderline top 20 position player in MLB this season.

Likelihood of Receiving Qualifying Offer: Probably 100 percent

The Cubs presumably aren't too interested in re-upping with Suzuki on another five-year deal. But if they can bring him back for one more season for not all that much more than what they had been paying him? They'd take that in a heartbeat.

Likelihood of Accepting Offer, If Extended: Probably zero percent

Suzuki turned 32 in August and probably isn't going to come all that close to the five-year, $150M contract that Kyle Schwarber signed at the same age last winter. But four years for $100M or even $110M is entirely feasible on the open market, given how consistently well he has hit the ball throughout his MLB career to date.

articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions following a dominant 2026 season where they finished with baseball's best record and rolled through the playoffs with an 11-2 record.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions following a dominant 2026 season where they finished with baseball's best record and rolled through the playoffs with an 11-2 record.

The focus now shifts to what promises to be a tumultuous offseason as the current CBA is set to expire on Dec. 1 and a lockout is widely expected. Before that happens, it's time for an updated version of our MLB power rankings to set the stage for what's to come this winter.

For our first reshuffling of these rankings, teams are ranked based on their 2027 outlook. That includes how complete the roster is heading into free agency, how active the club is expected to be in adding outside talent and the overall direction of the franchise.

We'll put together fresh versions of these power rankings throughout the offseason if and when the hot stove is re-lit. For now, this will serve as a baseline for those future editions of our leaguewide rankings.

2026 Opening Day Rank: 29 2026 Finish: 58-104, Fifth in NL West Key Free Agents: SP Kyle Freeland, SP Tomoyuki Sugano, SP José Quintana, RP Jordan Romano

Outlook: Another year, another MLB-worst ERA (5.59) from the Colorado pitching staff, and now they have to find a way to replace 66 starts and 337.2 innings in the starting rotation as Kyle Freeland, Tomoyuki Sugano and José Quintana hit free agency.

Will they cash in trade chips like Hunter Goodman and Jake McCarthy to try to acquire some viable arm talent, or just stick with the status quo despite four straight 100-loss seasons? Recent history says they'll be content to stay the course.

Key Free Agents: IF Adam Frazier, 3B Yoán Moncada

Outlook: The Angels went beyond just moving rentals at the deadline, trading José Soriano, Jo Adell and Ryan Zeferjahn for a haul of prospects and controllable young talent.

If they decide to lean into a long-overdue rebuild, shortstop Zach Neto and left-hander Reid Detmers could both bring back a blockbuster return, but they have stopped short of blowing things up time and again during their 12-year playoff drought.

Outlook: With Rafael Devers, Willy Adames, Matt Chapman and Jung Hoo Lee set to earn a combined $99.2 million in 2027, roughly half of the Giants' projected salary for next year is tied up in four players.

Shoring up the pitching staff behind Logan Webb will be the top priority this winter, which means those four bats will need to earn their money, with help from young slugger Bryce Eldridge, if an offense that ranked 26th in runs scored (669) is going to improve.

1 Player Every Team Must Re-Sign in Free Agency 💰

Way-Too-Early 2027 MLB Playoff Predictions 🔮

2026 Opening Day Rank: 23 2026 Finish: 64-98, Fourth in AL West

Key Free Agents: C Jonah Heim, 2B Jeff McNeil (club option), SP Jeffrey Springs (club option)

Outlook: The Athletics looked like a potential dark-horse contender entering the 2026 season thanks to a dynamic young offensive core, but almost every key bat in their lineup ended up missing time to injury.

They should be back to full strength to kick off the 2027 campaign, but it's now abundantly clear they need significant additions on the pitching side to have any shot at relevance. Their 5.51 ERA ranked 29th in the majors, and the starting staff turned in only 33 quality starts.

articles.title: Rays' Nick Martinez Reportedly Declines Contract Option, Will Hit MLB Free Agency After World Series
articles.summary: Coming off an All-Star appearance in 2026, Nick Martinez is headed for free agency.
articles.body:
Coming off an All-Star appearance in 2026, Nick Martinez is headed for free agency.

Per Jon Heyman of the New York Post and MLB Network, Martinez will decline his $20 million mutual option for 2027.

Martinez joined the Rays on a one-year deal worth a guaranteed $13 million in February 2026. The contract included a mutual option for 2027 with a $4 million buyout that will be paid by the club.

1 Player Every Team Must Re-Sign in Free Agency 💰

The deal turned out to be a steal in 2026, as Martinez put together arguably the best season of his career at the age of 35. He finished with a 3.10 ERA, setting career-highs in starts (31) and innings (180.0) in the regular season.

Tampa led the AL with 98 wins during the regular season to win the AL East for the first time since 2021. Martinez was given the ball for Game 1 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, allowing two runs in five innings in a 3-2 loss.

The Rays are normally tight with their payroll, so it will be interesting to see if they try to bring back Martinez given how much he can command on the open market.

Martinez opting out means the Rays are once again not on track to have an individual player make at least $15 million since Charlie Morton in 2019 and '20.

The strength of Tampa's roster during its run to the World Series last season was run prevention. Much of that could be attributed to a strong starting rotation, led by Martinez, Drew Rasmussen and Shane McClanahan.

Rasmussen and McClanahan remain under contract for 2027, so that unit should remain an asset for the Rays. Ryan Pepiot, who missed all of last season recovering from hip surgery, will likely be counted on to replace some of Martinez's production.

Martinez, meanwhile, will look to cash in with another contract as he enters his age-36 season. The right-hander is very reliable as a swing arm on any pitching staff because of his ability to start or cover multiple innings in relief.

articles.title: MLB World Series: Why did baseball’s biggest stage struggle for viewership?
articles.summary: When Brewers and Rays faced off, it marked the first World Series between two of MLB’s smallest spenders in 35 years.
articles.body:
The small-market World Series in Major League Baseball wrapped up this week, with the Milwaukee Brewers winning their first title in franchise history.

The title triumph came 44 years after Milwaukee’s only other trip to the Fall Classic, when they lost to the St Louis Cardinals in seven games in 1982.

But beyond the memorable victory, the series’ television ratings made for underwhelming reading, raising questions about baseball’s reach and relevance in a United States sports market dominated by American football and basketball.

Al Jazeera breaks down the numbers and more:

Who played in the 2026 MLB World Series?

The World Series, the championship series of the 2026 MLB season, saw the American League champion Tampa Bay Rays and the National League champion Milwaukee Brewers compete in a best-of-seven playoff series.

At the end of the October 23-28 playoff series, Milwaukee were crowned winners, as they clinched their first World Series title.

Milwaukee’s 57-year wait for a championship ended on Wednesday after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to wrap up the Fall Classic in five games.

Why didn’t the 2026 World Series capture TV audiences?

While the final Nielsen ratings report is still pending, estimates show an average of 11.82 million viewers tuned in for the 2026 World Series across the Fox network.

Milwaukee’s 10-1 win at Tampa in Game 3 attracted the lowest audience, 8.33 million, while Game 5, in which Milwaukee sealed the championship, drew the highest with 14.22 million viewers.

The overall average is much lower than the 2025 and 2024 World Series, which drew 15.49 million and 15.1 million viewers, respectively, as the Los Angeles Dodgers won the title both times.

This year’s World Series’ underwhelming viewership could be linked to the two teams’ relatively low payrolls and markets – the Brewers’ payroll ranks 19th in MLB ($146m), and the Rays are 28th ($95m).

The Brewers also rank as the smallest market team in MLB, generating the lowest local commercial and TV revenue, while the Rays rank squarely in the league’s middle.

Hence, when the Brewers and Rays met this year on MLB’s biggest stage, it marked the first World Series clash between two of baseball’s smallest spenders in 35 ⁠years.

On the other hand, nine-time World Series winners Dodgers, who competed in the last two World Series, boast a star-studded lineup on a hefty payroll, featuring marquee star Shohei Ohtani, former MVP Mookie Betts, 10-time All-Star Freddie Freeman and others.

Those factors keep them in the tier 1 market size category – one that represents the biggest media and population footprints in the sport.

How does the World Series compare with other US sports?

The 2026 World Series’ viewership figures also pale in comparison to those of other major US sports leagues.

Basketball’s 2026 NBA Finals, in which the New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 4-1 to end a 53-year drought, attracted a series average of 20.58 million viewers. Game 5 was the most-watched NBA Finals game 5 since 1998, averaging 24.54 million viewers and peaking at 33 million.

Elsewhere in international football, the 2026 FIFA World Cup, held in North America, also produced record numbers. Spain’s 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina delivered a combined average audience of 62.8 million across Fox and Telemundo, making it the most-watched football match ever in the United States.

American football, by far, is the most-watched sport in the US.

A Nielsen report found that an estimated 125.6 million viewers watched the National Football League’s Super Bowl LX, as the Seattle Seahawks beat the New England Patriots 29-13 .

NBC’s presentation of Super Bowl LX ranked as the second most-watched Super Bowl in history, behind the 127.7 million viewers who watched Super Bowl LIX in 2025.

The only major American sports league that performs weakly against MLB is the National Hockey League (NHL), a professional ice hockey league in North America.

An average of 5.2 million viewers tuned in for the 2026 Stanley Cup, won by the Carolina Hurricanes, who defeated the Vegas Golden Knights 4-2.

Why was the 2026 MLB London series cancelled?

MLB initially scheduled to host two games in London in mid-2026, with the New York Yankees and Toronto Blue Jays pencilled in to play on June 13 and 14 at London Stadium, the home ground of English football team West Ham United.

But the plan was cancelled due to scheduling issues with the venue and baseball’s television partner.

West Ham played their 2025-26 Premier League season’s final match against Leeds United at the ground on May 24, leaving very little time to convert the field to baseball, which can take up to three weeks.

Furthermore, MLB was unable to schedule games at the same venue later in June because Fox lacked available broadcast slots as that period clashed with the FIFA World Cup.

MLB games have been played abroad on several occasions, from Japan to Australia, since it was first played in Mexico in 2000.

MLB is also working on grassroots initiatives in India, known for its affinity for cricket, and last week hosted MLBx, a fast-paced 3-on-3 baseball competition that brought together baseball and softball stars.

Are other US sports leagues also held abroad?

Yes, major US sports leagues have made strides in expanding their international footprints, regularly hosting regular-season games, exhibition matches and special events abroad.

The NFL hosts regular-season games abroad in locations including London, Munich, Madrid, Sao Paulo and Mexico City.

Last month, the league expanded its presence with games in Melbourne, and the NFL’s first game Down Under drew 100,021 fans, making it the seventh most-attended regular-season game in NFL history.

With a large portion of the league’s player base and revenue coming from outside the US, the NBA also plays regular-season and preseason games in international cities like Paris, Abu Dhabi and Mexico City.

articles.title: Aaron Judge’s charitable work in MLB: How the New York Yankees captain uses his fame, ALL RISE Foundation, and community initiatives to support children, families, education, and youth leadership in 2026
articles.summary: Discover how Aaron Judge and his ALL RISE Foundation empower children and families with education, sports, leadership, and community support in New York and California.
articles.body: Aaron Judge is known for his power at the plate and his leadership as captain of the New York Yankees. But his impact also reaches communities beyond the baseball field. Through the ALL RISE Foundation, established in 2018, Judge has supported initiatives designed to help children develop confidence, strengthen their education and become responsible members of their communities. The organisation’s work focuses on practical opportunities that can help young people build skills and imagine broader possibilities for their futures.The foundation operates with a particular focus on the Bronx in New York City, while also supporting communities in California, including San Joaquin and Fresno counties. Its activities range from baseball camps and reading initiatives to leadership development, digital citizenship education and grants for local organisations. Rather than relying on one form of outreach, the foundation uses several programmes to connect young people with learning, mentorship and community resources.How Aaron Judge’s ALL RISE Foundation expands youth baseball, literacy, and digital safety programs in New York and CaliforniaThe ALL RISE Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit established by Judge to inspire children and young people to become responsible citizens. Its mission centres on encouraging leadership, education and character development through activities that help participants recognise their potential. The foundation is family-run, with Judge and his mother, Patty Judge, involved in its work.According to the foundation’s official website, its initiatives include mini-grants, aspiring leadership programmes, baseball camps, digital citizenship activities, reading projects and educational resources. These programmes reflect a broader approach to youth development: sports can encourage teamwork, reading can strengthen learning habits, and leadership activities can help students develop confidence and a sense of responsibility.By working with local organisations and youth programmes, ALL RISE helps connect Judge’s public profile with activities that can benefit children and families directly. Its work also reaches parts of California, extending its community support beyond New York.How Aaron Judge’s ALL RISE Foundation supports Bronx youthYouth baseball is one of the foundation’s most visible initiatives. Its camps give young players opportunities to practise skills, learn about teamwork and interact with people who have experience in the sport.In August 2026, Judge and former Yankees player Tyler Wade hosted a free Baseball ProCamp at Fordham University for 232 young players from nine Bronx Little League programmes. The camp included baseball drills, age-group races and team photographs. The foundation also donated $9,999.99 to help participating Little League programmes obtain equipment, according to reporting on the event.The camp illustrates how the foundation combines direct engagement with practical assistance. Children can learn in a supportive environment while community leagues receive help with equipment needs. Such contributions matter because organised sports can give young people structured activities, opportunities to cooperate and experiences that build discipline.The foundation’s involvement also helps draw attention to youth baseball programmes that may not have the same visibility as professional teams. While a single camp cannot address every barrier to participation, events and equipment support can help local organisations create more opportunities for children to take part.What Aaron Judge’s foundation funds across local communitiesThe foundation’s mini-grant programme supports organisations working with children and young people. Rather than limiting its work to baseball, ALL RISE backs community efforts that address different needs, including educational guidance, access to technology, inclusive learning and arts outreach. The goal is to help local groups deliver programmes that respond to the circumstances of the young people they serve.Organisations and initiatives associated with its community work include Children of Promise NYC and Bronx Horizons, which support young people through educational and future-planning opportunities; Birch Family Services and NYC Autism Charter Schools, which work with children with developmental and learning needs; and First Tech Fund, which focuses on digital access and technology opportunities. Arts outreach has also included support for the Fresno Philharmonic, while food-distribution efforts involving Second Harvest of the Greater Valley connect with wider community needs. Programme details and grant recipients can change over time, so individual funding claims should be checked against the foundation’s latest disclosures before publication.These partnerships reflect an important feature of the foundation’s approach: community support does not have to take one form. Educational guidance may help students plan for college or vocational training, technology access can open doors to digital learning, and inclusive services can support children who need tailored resources. Arts and food programmes address other dimensions of community life, including creative development and access to essential support.How Aaron Judge’s foundation promotes literacy and educationReading and learning are central to ALL RISE’s youth-development work. The Aaron Judge ALL RISE Book Club and the foundation’s reading initiatives encourage children to develop regular reading habits and engage with books beyond the classroom. The organisation also promotes resources such as its Leadership Library and educational webinars, giving young people additional ways to explore leadership and responsible citizenship.How ALL RISE supports digital safety and responsible citizenshipYoung people increasingly navigate online spaces for schoolwork, communication and entertainment. Digital safety education can help them recognise cyberbullying, protect personal information, evaluate online behaviour and make thoughtful decisions about what they share.
