articles.title: Top Videos, Photos from Brewers' World Series Parade After Historic Win vs. Rays
articles.summary: Two days after winning the first World Series title in franchise history, the Milwaukee Brewers got to celebrate with their home fans during a parade and rally on Friday.
articles.body:
Two days after winning the first World Series title in franchise history, the Milwaukee Brewers got to celebrate with their home fans during a parade and rally on Friday.

Knowing how big of an event this was for Brewers fans, Milwaukee officials closed all public schools in the city to give students a chance to celebrate.

The streets in downtown Milwaukee were packed with fans during the parade portion of the festivities.

Top Photos From Brewers' World Series Win

Brewers players were doing their part to help raise the energy, with Sal Frelick, Jacob Misiorowski and World Series MVP William Contreras firing up the crowd.

After the parade through the streets ended, everyone gathered at Henry Maier Festival Park for the rally where Brewers players and coaches got to share their thoughts about the season and fan support throughout this run.

Friday's celebration marks the culmination of the greatest season in Brewers history. They won a franchise-record 103 games during the regular season, marking the second consecutive year they have led MLB in victories.

Milwaukee followed that up with one of the most dominant playoff runs of all-time. The Brewers went 11-2 in October, tied for the third-best postseason record in history. They became the first team since the 2019 Washington Nationals to win eight consecutive postseason games.

It all led to Game 5 against the Rays on Wednesday night when four pitchers combined to allow four hits in a 4-1 victory to give Milwaukee its first championship in 58 seasons of existence.

articles.title: Sandy Alcantara's $21M Marlins Contract Option Exercised Ahead of MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: Former NL Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara is staying with the Miami Marlins, at least for now, after having his option for next season picked up.
articles.body:
Former NL Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara is staying with the Miami Marlins, at least for now, after having his option for next season picked up.

The Marlins officially announced on Friday they have exercised Alcantara's $21 million team option for 2027.

Marlins president of baseball operations Peter Bendix indicated during his end-of-season press conference on Sept. 29 he was anticipating Alcantara would remain with the club:

"He is so meaningful to this organization and that's not lost on me. Another incredible season. Really fun to watch him pitch, his leadership in the clubhouse, the way he handles himself and the way he sets an example for the rest of the team. It's second to none. It's something that I know Clayton really appreciates and I really appreciate. We value it tremendously."

The Marlins signed Alcantara to a five-year, $56 million extension in December 2021. He was coming off a strong season, then took a huge leap forward in 2022 to become one of the best pitchers in MLB.

Alcantara won the NL Cy Young award in 2022 after posting a 2.28 ERA in an MLB-leading 228.2 innings. His career hit a snag following that season because he struggle in 2023 with a 4.14 ERA before missing all of 2024 after undergoing Tommy John surgery.

After posting a career-high 5.36 ERA in 2025, Alcantara got back on track last season. He wasn't back to being a Cy Young contender, but his 3.87 ERA in an MLB-high 214.0 innings was very encouraging.

Even though the Marlins have picked up Alcantara's option, it's not a stretch to think the club could still look to move him before the start of the 2027 season. He received trade interest for him throughout the 2026 campaign, though they reportedly never sought to move him.

Given how tight Marlins ownership tends to be with the payroll, Alcantara's $21 million salary stands out on a roster that doesn't currently project to have another player making more than $5.1 million.

At the end of the 2026 regular season, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reported the Marlins don't plan on trading Alcantara this winter.

Alcantara, who will be 31 for most of next season, may not get back to being the ace that he was four years ago, but he remains incredibly valuable because of his ability to eat innings in an era when it's rare for anyone to reach the 200-inning threshold.

Accounting for the fact he missed an entire season, Alcantara still ranks in the top 20 among all starters in innings pitched since 2022.

Assuming the Marlins follow through with their reported stance of not trading him, Alcantara is a huge boost to their rotation because of his ability to take the ball every fifth day and go six quality innings in an era where so few pitchers are even asked to do that much.

articles.title: Brewers celebrate World Series title with parade through downtown Milwaukee
articles.summary: The Brewers clinched the franchise's first-ever World Series title on Wednesday against the Rays.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers' World Series celebrations continue on Friday as the team holds its championship parade .

To ensure students don't miss out on the memorable day, Milwaukee Public Schools announced that all schools and district offices are closed. The official reason is "due to operations and safety impacts from the Brewers parade and celebration," but there would likely be a lot of students cutting class to make their way downtown for the fun had classes remained in session.

After clinching the first title in franchise history on Wednesday night, members of the team were attendance to see the Green Bay Packers beat the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field on Thursday night. The Commissioner's Trophy was on hand for the festivities, which included Sal Frelick doing a Lambeau Leap.

Frelick remained in party mode Friday morning as the players got ready to take off.

Fans started lining up early and in numbers in order to get a good spot along the parade route, which will run through downtown Milwaukee and conclude at Henry Maier Festival Park.

It was not a surprise to learn that the beer lines were packed before the parade even started. It is Milwaukee, after all.

It wouldn't be a Brewers parade without remembering the late, great Bob Uecker.

The Brewers' mascots made sure to be in attendance as Bernie Brewer and Barrelman celebrated with the crowd.

And how many championship parades feature racing sausages?

Brewers fans have dressed up for the occasion.

Several former Brewers were part of the parade including Hall of Famer pitcher Rollie Fingers, who pitched for Milwaukee from 1981-85.

The Brewers have taken the stage at Henry Maier Festival Park and players are now addressing the crowd, beginning with team captain (and 2018 National League MVP) Christian Yelich.

"It's awesome, man," Yelich said. "Everybody's waited a really long time for this. We're just really excited that we could bring that trophy home in Milwaukee and share it with everybody that's out here today."

Maybe the loudest ovation was for World Series MVP William Contreras, who fired up an already raucous audience by yelling "Let's ****ing go, Brewers!"

Sal Frelick said "I'm gonna have a beer for every single person here!" Teammates and staff might want to check on him later, unless he maybe paces himself throughout the offseason.

Hitting coach Daniel Vogelbach provided musical entertainment by singing (or "singing") along to Fountains of Wayne's "Stacy's Mom."

Hall of Famer and Brewers legend Robin Yount rode Bob Uecker's Harley motorcycle on stage, which has to be some kind of nexus of Milwaukee sports mythology.

The parade and rally celebrations are wrapping up, but the Brewers and their fans will surely be reveling in the city's first World Series championship for days, weeks and months to come.
